newsitem.title: UK: Strong stg reflects confidence in govt - UK's Lang.
newsitem.headline: Strong stg reflects confidence in govt - UK's Lang.

text.p: The strength of sterling reflects market confidence in the British government's handling of the economy, Trade Secretary Ian Lang said on Monday.
Speaking on BBC radio, Lang acknowledged that the strong pound was a handicap to some exporters but said it was only one factor in determining competitiveness.

"A strong pound is a reflection of confidence in the government's handling of the eocnomy, and it is the confidence that would be put at risk with a new Labour government and all the threats they would bring in," he said.
Commenting on a warning by Oxford Economic Forecasting that the strong pound would curb British growth later this year, Lang said the manufacturing-led recovery was sustainable.
"That's what's so different about the recovery this time around," he said.

"A strong pound does of course create problems for some exporters. It also brings benefits, however, in terms of lower inflation -- cheaper raw materials prices -- and there are many other factors that come into play that affect our competitiveness," Lang said.
